quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: A bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is right because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as car drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance ramp:

options.text: Should let cars already on the highway go first.
May force their way into traffic.
Can expect other drivers to move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let cars already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you must yield to cars already on the highway. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small vehicle, be ready for:

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Be ready to steer carefully when passing or driving near large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You should:

options.text: You have done all you can.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: Drivers should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are harder to spot than cars because they are smaller and have less visible lights. Always stay alert for these smaller road users to avoid crashes.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check for blind spots.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no cars are in your blind spot. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: At night when a car is coming toward you, your headlights should be:
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another car is coming toward you or when you are following another car. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle sign is an orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. You should:

options.text: Wait for the car to pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the car to pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Don't try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Don't let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If cars are backing up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off to the right and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to see if another car is following too close. Slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because a driver is following too close.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related car crashes?

options.text: Decide not to drive before you start drinking.
Tell someone "No thanks, I'm driving" if they offer you a drink.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you won't drive. Alcohol makes it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a car on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open bottle anywhere in the car, whether you are driving or not.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens, you must immediately:

options.text: Move to the right and stop.
Move to the right and slow down.
Move to the right and turn on your flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights, sirens, or warning devices, move to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are near the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to others, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, make sure the lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a worker tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when told by a worker, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you of an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready to stop for red or yellow lights and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign warns you about:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn about hazards on the road. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way to turn left when you see:
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, you should:

options.text: Calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions distract you from driving. Your mind focuses on your feelings instead of the road. Take time to calm down and focus before you drive.

questions.question: A stop sign has the shape of a(n):
questions.explanation: Only stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). This shape tells you to make a complete stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows you the only direction traffic can move on this road.

questions.question: Defensive driving means:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify danger before it happens and act to prevent accidents. It helps you avoid crashes with bad, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop at all eight-sided red signs.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually once the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right lane if available. If not, slow down gradually once ahead is clear to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give you instructions.
They may follow each other closely.

questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. They have the right-of-way when using sirens or lights. Follow any loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the road is clear.

questions.question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and SUVs have bigger blind spots. These are areas near the rear that the driver cannot see in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not lower your BAC.
